nodes.label: byRank
nodes.doc: Static beats `:param` beats a pattern that has ENDED beats `*`, position by position; an equal pattern goes to the deeper route, so an index child wins over the layout it shares a path with.

nodes.label: collectExoRouteGuards
nodes.doc: ONE ROUTE, not its branch: the caller walks the chain and collects per entry, so an ancestor's `beforeEnter` runs before its child's in the order the chain already holds.

nodes.label: emptyQueryRecord
nodes.doc: NOT `{}`: twelve keys already have answers there, so `?constructor=1` and `?__proto__=x` both take the repeated-key branch on a value that was never a query value.

nodes.label: ensureSearchPrefix
nodes.doc: Named for its direction: `query.ts` has a private `normalizeSearch` that takes the `?` OFF.

nodes.label: executeExoGuards
nodes.doc: SHORT-CIRCUITS on the first answer that is not `true`, and returns THAT answer: a string is a redirect target, and running the remaining guards would discard it.

nodes.label: EXO_ROUTER
nodes.doc: ONE token for the process: two would be two identities and the outlet would find nothing.

nodes.label: exoOutlet
nodes.doc: CALL IT AT MODULE LEVEL: it builds a schema, numbered and compiled once, so calling it per render recompiles an unchanged shape and defeats every per-schema cache underneath.

nodes.label: ExoOutlet
nodes.doc: The `<div>` outlet, built ONCE at module load.

nodes.label: fetchExoRouteChunk
nodes.doc: Warms the cache and NOTHING more — it never inspects what the module exported and stores nothing a synchronous render can read, which is the whole difference from `preloadExoPage`.

nodes.label: injectExoRouter
nodes.doc: THROWS where `c.inject` would answer `undefined`: with no router an outlet shows nothing and a link cannot resolve an href, and both would fail later with nothing naming the missing provide.

nodes.label: isAbsoluteUrl
nodes.doc: Its own scheme or authority — `https://…`, `mailto:…`, `//host/x`.

nodes.label: isExoPageMachine
nodes.doc: The other member of the union is a LOADER, which is a function, so these two fields are the whole test.

nodes.label: joinExoPaths
nodes.doc: A child path beginning with `/` is ABSOLUTE and ignores its parent — that is how a nested route escapes its branch.

nodes.label: LINK_SCHEMA
nodes.doc: A real `<a href>`, because the markup is what a crawler follows and what "open in a new tab" opens.

nodes.label: LOADING
nodes.doc: The in-flight load per loader, so n outlets asking at once fetch one chunk.

nodes.label: matchExoRouteChain
nodes.doc: The full matched branch, root → leaf.

nodes.label: normalizeExoPathname
nodes.doc: One leading slash, no repeated slashes, no trailing slash except at the root.

nodes.label: normalizeSearch
nodes.doc: `URLSearchParams` wants it off; `ensureSearchPrefix` puts it back.

nodes.label: parseExoPath
nodes.doc: Hash is cut FIRST: a `?` after a `#` is part of the fragment, not the query.

nodes.label: preloadExoPage
nodes.doc: Awaiting this before a server render is what makes a lazy route printable: a render is one synchronous call, so a route still holding a `() => import(…)` prints an empty region.

nodes.label: provideExoRouter
nodes.doc: A function, not a provider component: a component is exactly ONE element, so it would have to invent a wrapper node to carry a value that needs none.

nodes.label: RESOLVED
nodes.doc: `loadExoLazyMachine` caches the PROMISE; this caches the VALUE, which is the half a synchronous render can read.

nodes.label: resolvedPage
nodes.doc: Internal: a caller outside this package wanting the component should hold it as a module import.

nodes.label: resolveExoHref
nodes.doc: SHARED because two histories disagreeing about hrefs would put one URL in an `ExoLink`'s markup and send `navigate` to another — visible only under a base path, and only in one of the two.

nodes.label: resolveExoRouteMachine
nodes.doc: A chain, not one `await`: a loader whose module exports another loader is resolved too.

nodes.label: resolvePath
nodes.doc: A `*` catch-all segment is left as-is: its param name is route-local.

nodes.label: sameMatch
nodes.doc: A commit hands an unchanged level its PREVIOUS match object when this says equal, which is what lets a route boundary compare levels with `===`.

nodes.label: shouldIgnoreExoLinkClick
nodes.doc: A ROUTER MAY ONLY INTERCEPT A PLAIN LEFT CLICK ON AN INTERNAL DESTINATION — every other case here is something the user meant, and swallowing it is a bug they cannot work around.

nodes.label: showExoOutletRoute
nodes.doc: Only the match moved: a page with a wire is RE-WIRED with it, one without is rebuilt.

nodes.label: stringifyExoQuery
nodes.doc: An empty record gives the EMPTY STRING, not a bare `?`, so the result concatenates onto a pathname.

nodes.label: subscribeExoHistory
nodes.doc: One subscription policy for both histories.
